articles.title: Welcome to Emerald: Legends
articles.summary: A guide to the project, its identity, and what is currently playable.
articles.content:
## What is Pokémon Emerald: Legends?
Pokémon Emerald: Legends is an unofficial, non-commercial ROM hack built on rh-hideout's pokeemerald-expansion. It keeps Emerald's Hoenn story at its core, adding optional quality-of-life features, trainer customization, seasons, and an expanding Champion-era Kanto journey.

This wiki is a **player-focused snapshot**, reviewed when the project owner requests an update. It is not automatically rewritten each time the ROM receives a release.

## New here?
- [[walkthrough|Follow the story walkthrough from New Game]].
- [[install|Install and patch the game]] with a legally obtained, clean compatible Emerald ROM.
- [[builds|Choose Release or Debug]].
- [[options|Explore the three Options pages]] before starting a new save.
- [[kanto|Discover Kanto]] after becoming Champion.

## Current playable scope
Hoenn retains its recognizable main adventure. Kanto has a playable southeastern and central route network, two visiting Gym challenges, an introductory Wing Survey, and a permanent ferry from Lilycove. The remainder of the Kanto Gym circuit and the planned legendary encounters **are not yet playable**.

## Finding information
Use the search field, browse sections on the left, or select any linked article. Each article has its own shareable URL. This site does not require accounts, registration, or login.

articles.title: Installation and browser patching
articles.summary: Get the playable game onto an emulator without uploading your original ROM.
articles.content:
## What you need
- A legally obtained clean **Pokémon Emerald (US/Europe)** ROM that matches SHA-1 `f3ae088181bf583e55daf962a92bb46f4f1d07b7`.
- A modern emulator capable of running Game Boy Advance games.
- The project’s [[builds|Release or Debug]] BPS patch, or the built-in browser patcher.

## Recommended: local browser patcher
1. Visit [the official browser patcher](../patcher.html).
2. Select **Release** for normal gameplay, or Debug only if you need developer controls.
3. Select your own clean Emerald ROM from your device.
4. The patcher validates the original and creates your patched `.gba` **in your browser**.
5. Save that new file and open it with a GBA emulator.

**Privacy:** the original ROM stays on your device. It is not uploaded to the project site.

## Alternative: BPS patch
Download the matching BPS file from [the official downloads page](../index.html#downloads) and apply it locally using a reputable BPS patcher against the same clean ROM.

## Saves and updates
Keep a backup of your emulator save file before switching game builds. Release and Debug carry the same gameplay content, but Debug includes extra testing commands that can change progress. Test major changes on a backup.

## Troubleshooting
A ROM checksum mismatch usually means the wrong game, region, revision, or a previously patched ROM. Do not rename a file to make it appear compatible. Start with the specified clean original.

articles.title: Release and Debug builds
articles.summary: What the two downloadable variants actually change.
articles.content:
## Release — recommended
Release is intended for ordinary players. It contains every shipped Legends gameplay and content addition without developer-only shortcuts.

## Debug — for testing
Debug contains the same gameplay and story but keeps tools available in the expansion, such as overworld and battle debug menus, Pokémon sprite inspection, and title-screen Quickstart where supported.

## Which should I use?
- Choose **Release** for your primary adventure.
- Choose **Debug** for checking encounters, maps, graphics, and reporting reproducible bugs.

These are two builds from one source revision. **Release is not vanilla Emerald**: vanilla Emerald means the untouched commercial original.

Find both options on the [main downloads page](../index.html#downloads). Public downloads are BPS patches, not redistributed commercial ROMs.

articles.title: Game walkthrough: start your adventure
articles.summary: Follow your Hoenn adventure from New Game through the Pokémon League, with maps, catches and clear story checkpoints.
articles.content:
## Start here
This walkthrough follows **Pokémon Emerald: Legends v0.0.31.1**, checked on **10 October 2026**. It covers the main Hoenn story, with Legends-specific changes explained at the point you meet them.

Read in order, or jump to the chapter matching your location. Story instructions contain spoilers for that chapter. Optional stops and suggested preparation are labeled separately from required progress.

## Your first adventure
**Starting a new save?** Begin with [[walkthrough-littleroot|Chapter 1: Littleroot and your first Pokémon]]. Follow its numbered steps in order. Already playing? Choose your current town or stop above to jump directly to the relevant instructions.

## New to Pokémon?
- **Directions:** North means toward the top of the game screen, south means down, west means left and east means right.
- **Healing:** Speak to the nurse at a Pokémon Center to restore your party's HP and moves. Healing is free, and you can return as often as you need.
- **Catching:** You receive Poké Balls after the first rival battle and laboratory visit. Weaken a wild Pokémon without making it faint, then choose a Poké Ball from your Bag. You cannot catch another trainer's Pokémon.
- **Battles:** If an opponent is difficult, heal, gain a few levels against nearby wild Pokémon or trainers, and try again. The suggested levels in these chapters are helpful targets, not requirements.
- **Saving:** Use SAVE from the game's Start menu after important progress and before a Gym battle. The wiki does not save or control your game.
- **Required or optional?** Numbered story instructions move you forward. Stops marked **Optional** can be skipped; you do not need to catch every suggested Pokémon.

## Keep LegendsDex handy
Use [Routes in LegendsDex](./dex.html?view=routes) to find catches along the way, or [the National Pokédex](./dex.html?view=species) to look up a Pokémon. Tap a sprite to hear its cry; tap its name for stats, encounter locations and highlighted maps. Inside the detail card, tap the name again for its Pokédex entry. The Shiny button beside its category label previews the game’s shiny colors; tap again to return to normal.

The encounter catalogue is a separately maintained snapshot. It lists standard wild tables, so gift Pokémon and special story encounters need their own instructions. This walkthrough does not silently update that catalogue.

## How to use the advice
The suggested training levels are preparation tips, not level caps or mandatory requirements. Your starter, moves, caught team and EXP Share setting can change how difficult a battle feels. Heal and save before important fights, and adapt your team when a suggested Pokémon is not one you want to use.

Release and Debug share these story steps. For a regular playthrough, [[builds|Release is the recommended build]]. Debug shortcuts can skip events the walkthrough expects you to complete normally.

## After the Hoenn League
These fourteen chapters cover the main Hoenn journey. Optional Hoenn areas and Legends' current Kanto postgame remain available after the ending; see [[kanto|the Kanto overview]] for entry instructions and the current scope. Further postgame walkthrough chapters will be added through manual reviews.

**This guide is updated only when the project owner requests a review.** A new game release does not automatically rewrite these chapters. See [[about|the wiki's update policy]].

articles.title: Chapter 1: Littleroot and your first Pokémon
articles.summary: Choose your settings, settle into Littleroot, rescue the Professor, and unlock catching and DexNav.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Rescue the Professor, beat your rival on Route 103, then return to the Littleroot laboratory to unlock catching. Finish by collecting Running Shoes from Mom.

**First time playing?** Keep this chapter open and follow one section at a time. Use the town selector above when you want to return to a specific stop. [[walkthrough|See the beginner tips and all walkthrough stops]].

## Before choosing New Game
If you still need to patch the game, follow [[install|the installation guide]] first. Use the Release build for ordinary play, then open **Options** before selecting New Game.

On the **Adventure** page, choose your STARTERS setting. GEN 3 gives Treecko, Torchic and Mudkip; generations 1–9 offer their own starter trios. SPECIAL offers Happiny, Wattrel and Mankey. RANDOM offers three distinct eligible unevolved Pokémon. [[starters|See the full starter list]].

On the **Legends** page, review EXP Share, followers, shiny odds and seasons. EXP Share starts enabled for a new save and has a matching Key Item. These are personal preferences; you do not need a particular shiny rate or season to follow the story. [[options|Options controls and page navigation]].

**Make your starter-set choice before opening the rescue bag on Route 101.** That first opening fixes the lineup and the rival's starter lineage for this save. Changing the setting afterward does not replace a Pokémon you already chose.

## Arriving in Littleroot
1. Start New Game and complete Professor Birch's introduction. Choose your trainer, skin tone, outfit and name using the preview.
2. Leave the moving truck and follow Mom into your house.
3. Go upstairs and inspect your bedroom clock. Choose **REAL TIME** to follow the emulator/device clock, or **MANUAL** to set the time yourself. Confirm the choice to complete the clock scene.
4. Return downstairs and finish the television conversation with Mom.
5. Visit the other house in town. Go upstairs and inspect the Poké Ball to meet your rival, May or Brendan.

You can revisit your own clock later to change its mode. The rival's clock is view-only. If your emulator has no usable real-time clock, Legends has a saved playtime-based fallback; see [[clock|the clock guide]].

**Optional:** Your bedroom wardrobe lets you change outfits and accessories later, with footwear and Trainer Card colors in their own categories. You can return whenever you want a new look. [[wardrobe|Wardrobe guide]].

## Rescue on Route 101
Leave Littleroot through the northern exit. The Professor needs help on Route 101. Interact with his nearby bag and choose one of the three Pokémon.

The rescue battle in this Legends build is against a **level 2 Stunky**. Use the attacks your starter already knows. After the rescue, the story returns you to the laboratory, where the Professor lets you keep your starter and offers a nickname.

Your next objective is to meet the rival on Route 103. Accept the invitation, leave the lab, and travel north through Route 101 into Oldale Town.

## Oldale and the first rival battle
Heal at Oldale's Pokémon Center before heading north. **Optional:** Speak to the Poké Mart employee outside for the shop introduction and a free Potion.

Follow the northern exit to Route 103 and talk to your rival. Their first partner is **level 5**. With a generation starter set, they use that generation's counter starter. SPECIAL and RANDOM use Zorua instead.

**Suggested preparation:** A healthy starter around level 6–8 and a Potion give you some breathing room. If your current moves struggle, battle nearby wild Pokémon for experience, heal again, and return. Catching supplies arrive after this event, so you do not need to assemble a wild-caught team first.

After winning, follow the rival's directions back through Oldale and Route 101 to the laboratory in Littleroot.

## National Pokédex, Poké Balls and Running Shoes
1. Complete the laboratory conversation. The first Pokédex gift is already the **National Pokédex** in Legends.
2. DexNav unlocks at the same event. It can be selected from the Start menu once the conversation finishes.
3. Your rival gives you **five Poké Balls**. You can now begin catching wild Pokémon.
4. Leave the laboratory and complete Mom's departure conversation outside. She gives you the **Running Shoes**; hold B while moving to run.
5. Save, then head north to Oldale again. Its western route is now your path toward Petalburg.

## A gift already waiting in storage
**Optional:** Check Pokémon storage at a Pokémon Center PC. Legends places one **level 5 Da Bug** in the first available storage slot when a new game begins. Withdraw it if you want the custom Bug-type in your team; it does not appear in the ordinary wild tables.

Da Bug begins with Tackle, Leer, Mean Look and Absorb. Its separate shiny roll is 1 in 10. This gift is independent of your starter choice. [[da-bug|More about Da Bug]].

## Ready for Chapter 2
You should have your starter, the National Pokédex, DexNav, Poké Balls and Running Shoes. Your next destination is **Route 102, west of Oldale**.

**Next: [[walkthrough-petalburg|Chapter 2: your first team and Petalburg Woods]].** Return to [[walkthrough|the walkthrough index]].

Checked against game v0.0.31.1 on 10 October 2026. The encounter catalogue remains its existing manual snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 2: Your first team and Petalburg Woods
articles.summary: Catch your first partners, meet Norman and Wally, then cross the woods toward Rustboro.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Visit Norman in Petalburg Gym and complete Wally's catching tutorial. Then travel west onto Route 104 and north through Petalburg Woods to Rustboro.

**First time playing?** Keep this chapter open and follow one section at a time. Use the town selector above when you want to return to a specific stop. [[walkthrough|See the beginner tips and all walkthrough stops]].

## From Oldale to Route 102
Continue from [[walkthrough-littleroot|Chapter 1]] by taking Oldale's western exit. Route 102 leads to Petalburg City and introduces ordinary trainer battles along the path.

Weaken wild Pokémon before throwing a Poké Ball, and heal at Oldale if your team runs low. Trainer-owned Pokémon cannot be caught.

**Optional early catches:** Route 102's indexed grass encounters include Lotad, Seedot, Ralts, Poochyena, Wurmple and Zigzagoon. Lotad can offer Water and Grass coverage; Seedot is another Grass-type option. Ralts is a less common encounter, so you do not need to wait for one to keep moving. Use [Route 102 in LegendsDex](./dex.html?map=MAP_ROUTE102) for the listed levels and encounter shares.

## Make use of Legends' early tools
- **EXP Share:** The Key Item and Options toggle control party-wide experience. Keep it on to develop newly caught partners while your main battler handles trainers, or switch it off if you prefer more direct training. [[exp|How EXP Share works]].
- **DexNav:** Open it from the Start menu near valid encounter terrain, such as this route's grass. An upper-left instruction window explains when there is no usable search area. Targets allow up to 45 seconds; walking, running or cycling toward them does not itself make them flee. Range loss, leaving the map, cancellation or timeout can still end a search. [[dexnav|DexNav guide]].
- **Adventure Log:** Open ADVENTURE LOG in the Start menu to check recorded milestones and recent field notes. It is useful for remembering your last stop after a break. [[journal|Notebook controls]].

## Meet Norman and help Wally
1. Enter Petalburg City and heal at its Pokémon Center.
2. Visit the Gym and talk to your father, **Norman**.
3. Follow the scene in which Wally asks for a Pokémon and you accompany him for the catching tutorial.
4. Return to the Gym and finish Norman's directions.

You do **not** battle Norman for a badge on this first visit. He asks you to return after earning four badges; your first Gym destination is Rustboro.

After the scene, take Petalburg's western exit onto the southern part of Route 104.

## Route 104 and the woods
Travel north along Route 104 and enter Petalburg Woods. Mr. Briney's cottage is on the southern stretch near the coast; make a note of it for later, when you will return for a boat ride.

Follow the walkable forest path north. Battle trainers for experience and collect items you can reach. Small trees block optional paths at this stage; you can return after earning the Stone Badge.

**Optional team stop:** Shroomish appears in the woods' standard grass encounters and gives you another Grass-type option for the first Gym. Wurmple, Silcoon, Cascoon, Slakoth, Taillow and Poochyena are also indexed here. [Petalburg Woods encounters](./dex.html?map=MAP_PETALBURG_WOODS).

## The first Team Aqua encounter
Partway through the woods, a Devon researcher looking for Shroomish is threatened by a Team Aqua grunt. Help him by winning the battle.

The grunt uses a **level 9 Poochyena**. A healthy team around level 10–12 is a comfortable suggestion, rather than a requirement. Heal or use a Potion beforehand if earlier trainer battles have worn you down.

After the grunt leaves, the researcher gives you a **Great Ball** and mentions trouble involving Rustboro. Finish the conversation, then continue north out of the woods.

## Northern Route 104
The woods exit puts you on the northern stretch of Route 104. Follow the road and bridge toward Rustboro, dealing with trainers along the way. Have two healthy Pokémon ready for any double battle you choose to take.

**Optional stops:**
- Speak to the boy on this stretch for **TM Bullet Seed**. It can provide a Grass attack to a compatible team member.
- Visit the **Pretty Petal Flower Shop** for the **Wailmer Pail**, used to water berry plants.
- Collect available berries and explore reachable side paths, then continue north into Rustboro City.

## Ready for Chapter 3
Heal at Rustboro's Pokémon Center and save. Review whether your team has a usable Water, Grass or Fighting attack before visiting Roxanne's Rock-type Gym.

**Next: [[walkthrough-rustboro|Chapter 3: Rustboro, Roxanne and the Devon rescue]].** Previous: [[walkthrough-littleroot|Littleroot and your first Pokémon]]. Return to [[walkthrough|the walkthrough index]].

Checked against game v0.0.31.1 on 10 October 2026. Catch lists link to the existing manually maintained LegendsDex catalogue.

articles.title: Chapter 3: Rustboro, Roxanne and the Devon rescue
articles.summary: Earn the Stone Badge, recover the stolen Devon Parts, and prepare for your first boat journey.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Earn the Stone Badge, rescue Peeko in Rusturf Tunnel, and return the Devon Parts. Then visit Mr. Briney's cottage on southern Route 104 for the boat to Dewford.

**First time playing?** Keep this chapter open and follow one section at a time. Use the town selector above when you want to return to a specific stop. [[walkthrough|See the beginner tips and all walkthrough stops]].

## Prepare in Rustboro
Arrive from northern Route 104 after [[walkthrough-petalburg|Chapter 2]]. Heal, buy any Potions or Poké Balls you need, and save before entering the Gym.

**Optional:** Visit the Cutter's house for **HM Cut**. Legends' field utility is unlocked by the Stone Badge without requiring you to teach Cut to a party Pokémon. You can still collect the HM for its battle move. [[field|Badge-based field moves]].

Roxanne uses Rock-type Pokémon. Water and Grass attacks are particularly effective against her Geodude, while Water, Grass and Fighting attacks can help against Nosepass. If you chose a Fire starter, bring supporting coverage rather than relying only on Fire attacks.

**Suggested preparation:** A main battler around level 14–16, a healthy backup and a few healing items are a comfortable starting point. This is advice, not a required level. Lotad from Route 102 or Shroomish from Petalburg Woods are possible supporting catches; check their current moves instead of assuming their type alone guarantees an attack you need.

## Roxanne and the Stone Badge
Work through the Gym trainers and speak to Roxanne when you are ready. Her first team in this build is:

| Pokémon | Level | Watch for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Geodude | 12 | Defense Curl, Rock Throw and Rock Tomb |
| Geodude | 12 | A second copy of the same team member |
| Nosepass | 15 | Held Oran Berry, Harden, Block and Rock Tomb |

Roxanne also has **two Potions**. Rock Tomb can lower Speed, Harden can make physical attacks less effective, and Block can prevent a switch. Use your strongest suitable attacks and heal before your active Pokémon is in danger of fainting.

After winning, finish the reward conversation to receive the **Stone Badge** and **TM Rock Tomb**. In Legends, this badge unlocks the Cut field utility: interact with a small cuttable tree without needing an HM moveslot.

Save after the victory. Norman is still a later objective; one badge is not enough to challenge him yet.

## Follow the Devon theft
Leaving the Gym advances the Rustboro story. A Team Aqua grunt has stolen Devon's goods. Speak to the Devon employee and take the city's eastern route onto **Route 116**.

Follow Route 116 east toward **Rusturf Tunnel**. Fight trainers or explore as you like, but the tunnel entrance is your story destination. Mr. Briney reports that the thief has also taken his Wingull, **Peeko**.

**Optional catches:** Route 116's indexed grass encounters include Nincada, Abra, Skitty, Whismur, Taillow and Poochyena. You can use this route to fill out your team before or after the rescue. [Route 116 encounters](./dex.html?map=MAP_ROUTE116).

## Rescue Peeko in Rusturf Tunnel
1. Enter the tunnel from Route 116 and approach the grunt holding Peeko.
2. Defeat the Team Aqua grunt.
3. Finish the conversation to recover the **Devon Parts**.
4. Watch Mr. Briney reunite with Peeko, then leave the tunnel and return west to Rustboro.

You do not need to clear the rocks that block the full tunnel crossing for this rescue. Completing that connection is a later field-move task.

## Devon Corporation and your delivery jobs
Return to the Devon employee in Rustboro. He gives you another **Great Ball** and takes you to the company's president, **Mr. Stone**.

Complete the office conversation. You receive **Steven's Letter** and the **PokéNav**, and your party is healed. Your next jobs are to deliver the letter to Steven in Dewford and carry the Devon Parts onward to Slateport.

Leave Devon Corporation and complete the PokéNav/Match Call introduction outside. If your rival offers a Rustboro battle, you can accept for practice or decline and continue toward the boat.

**For later:** After delivering Steven's letter, return to Mr. Stone for a **Lucky Egg**. Legends gives this in place of the original Devon EXP Share reward; your EXP Share Key Item was already available at the start. [[exp|EXP Share and Lucky Egg]].

## Reach the boat for Dewford
Travel south from Rustboro through northern Route 104, Petalburg Woods and the southern stretch of Route 104. Visit **Mr. Briney's cottage** by the coast and talk to him.

With Peeko rescued and the Devon meeting complete, he offers to sail to **Dewford**. Heal and save before leaving if you want a clean checkpoint for the next leg of your journey.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Stone Badge earned and Roxanne's reward conversation finished.
- Peeko rescued and Devon Parts recovered.
- Mr. Stone's meeting completed; Steven's Letter and PokéNav received.
- PokéNav introduction completed outside Devon Corporation.
- Mr. Briney available at his Route 104 cottage for the trip to Dewford.

You are ready for [[walkthrough-dewford|Chapter 4: Dewford, Brawly and Steven]]. Use the Next chapter button below to continue.

Previous: [[walkthrough-petalburg|your first team and Petalburg Woods]]. Return to [[walkthrough|the walkthrough index]].

Checked against game v0.0.31.1 on 10 October 2026. Battle strategy and training levels are recommendations; progression and reward details were checked against the current scripts.

articles.title: Chapter 4: Dewford, Brawly and Steven
articles.summary: Earn the Knuckle Badge, explore Granite Cave and deliver Steven’s Letter.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Arrive by Mr. Briney's boat, earn your second badge and deliver the letter to Steven in Granite Cave. Finish by asking Mr. Briney to sail to Slateport.

Keep **Steven's Letter** and the **Devon Parts** with you. They are separate deliveries: Steven is near Dewford; Captain Stern is in Slateport. You do not need to discard either item or teach an HM to make progress.

## Arrive in Dewford
1. Heal at the Pokémon Center and save after the boat ride.
2. **Optional:** Speak to the fisherman in town for the **Old Rod**. Fish from a suitable water edge by using the rod from your Bag. This adds a new way to catch Pokémon; it is not required to reach Steven.
3. Walk north onto Route 106 to find Granite Cave's entrance. Route 107 is the surrounding sea route, not a road you can walk to Slateport.

Dewford's shops and services differ from a large city. Bring the healing supplies you bought in Rustboro, or use Mr. Briney's boat if you need to revisit the mainland.

## Brawly and the Knuckle Badge
Visit Dewford Gym. Its dark view expands as you defeat Gym trainers. Follow the visible paths and speak to trainers rather than treating the dark areas as missing map graphics.

Brawly specializes in Fighting Pokémon. Flying and Psychic attacks are useful options; an available Fairy attack can also help in Legends. Check actual moves and secondary types rather than relying on a type label alone. A healthy team around **level 18–20** is a suggested starting point. Normal, Rock and Dark partners can be vulnerable to Fighting attacks.

Heal and save before the leader. Winning earns the **Knuckle Badge** and **TM Bulk Up**. The badge unlocks **Flash** as a Legends field utility. Use the party's **FIELD** menu in a dark cave; no Pokémon needs a Flash moveslot. [[field|How field utilities work]].

## Granite Cave and the letter
1. Enter Granite Cave from Route 106. Speak to the hiker near the entrance for **HM Flash** if you want to collect it; the badge already supplies its field use.
2. Follow the cave's ladders into the lower floors. Use FIELD → Flash if visibility is poor, and keep track of ladders you have already used.
3. Continue through the lower cave and the path back toward Steven's room. Bike-only side paths are optional; they are not the letter-delivery route.
4. Speak to Steven and finish the conversation. He takes the letter, gives **TM Steel Wing** and registers his PokéNav contact.
5. Return to the entrance, heal in Dewford and save.

The cave has its own encounters on each floor. The inline lists below distinguish those floors, so a Pokémon listed downstairs is not necessarily on the entrance floor. Repels can make the return trip easier if your team is already prepared.

## Optional return to Devon
After delivering the letter, Mr. Stone in Rustboro rewards you with a **Lucky Egg**. This replaces the original game's EXP Share reward; Legends already provides its EXP Share Key Item at the start. You can make this return trip now or later. It is not required before sailing to Slateport.

## Ready for Slateport
Speak to Mr. Briney by the boat and choose Slateport once the delivery permits the next trip.

- Knuckle Badge earned; Flash utility available.
- Steven's Letter delivered and Steven's conversation completed.
- Devon Parts still ready for Captain Stern.
- Team healed before departure.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 5: Slateport and the road to Mauville
articles.summary: Deliver the Devon Parts, stop Team Aqua at the museum and cross Route 110.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Deliver the Devon Parts to Captain Stern in Slateport, then travel north along Route 110 to Mauville. The museum event opens the next part of your journey.

## Route 109 and Slateport
Mr. Briney's boat lands on Route 109's beach. Walk north into Slateport and find the Pokémon Center before exploring. Beach trainers and reachable items are optional; take them at your own pace.

**Optional:** Visit the market for supplies and browse the city's other attractions. The Battle Tent, contests and fan club are side activities, not requirements for the next badge. Keep enough healing items for two museum battles and the route ahead.

## Find Captain Stern
1. Enter **Stern's Shipyard**, in the southeastern part of the city.
2. Speak to **Dock** on the ground floor. He explains that Captain Stern is at the Oceanic Museum.
3. Leave the shipyard and enter the **Oceanic Museum**. The normal entry fee is **₽50**; the story admission script also lets you through if you lack the money while the delivery is still pending.
4. Go upstairs and speak to Captain Stern.
5. Defeat the Team Aqua grunts who interrupt the delivery. Keep your active Pokémon healthy between battles.
6. Complete the scene with Archie and Stern. The Devon Parts are handed over during the event.

**Optional:** A familiar grunt downstairs gives **TM Thief**. Collect it before leaving if you want the move. If the story route remains blocked afterward, return upstairs and ensure Stern's final conversation finished.

## Route 110 and your rival
Take Slateport's northern exit. The road leads under and beside Cycling Road; you can follow the ground route without owning a bike. The Trick House is an optional puzzle stop near the start.

Your rival waits farther along Route 110. Heal before approaching the encounter and save if you want a retry checkpoint. This battle checks whether your team has grown beyond its starter: bring a partner that can handle the rival's starter matchup and avoid arriving with several fainted Pokémon.

A main team around **level 20–22** is a preparation suggestion. The rival's starter lineage follows your New Game choice; the original Emerald starter assumption does not cover Special or Random saves.

After the battle, finish the conversation, then continue north. Collect reachable items and train against route trainers if needed. The wild list below shows this route's standard catches, not the rival's team.

## First steps in Mauville
Enter Mauville, heal and save. You have reached the city for your third Gym Badge, but do not rush straight into a leader battle with a worn-out team.

**Optional nearby detour:** Route 117 west of Mauville leads to Verdanturf and the Day Care area. You can explore it for catches and training before the Gym, then return to Mauville.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Dock spoken to and Stern found upstairs in the museum.
- Aqua interruption cleared and Devon Parts delivered.
- Route 110 rival battle completed.
- Mauville reached with a healthy party.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 6: Mauville and Wattson
articles.summary: Get a bike, prepare for Electric attacks and earn the Dynamo Badge.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Complete Wally's encounter outside Mauville Gym, defeat Wattson and use the newly unlocked Rock Smash utility to head north.

## Explore Mauville
Heal and save at the Pokémon Center. Visit **Rydel's bike shop** for a free bike: the **Mach Bike** is built for speed and slopes, while the **Acro Bike** handles tricks and certain side paths. You can return to exchange them, so this is not a permanent save choice.

**Optional:** Collect **HM Rock Smash** from the man in Mauville's house. Legends unlocks its overworld use through the Dynamo Badge without requiring the HM or a taught move. Collecting the HM remains useful if you want its battle move.

Check your team before the Gym. Route 117 to the west and the accessible part of Route 118 to the east are training and catching options. You cannot cross Route 118's water yet; Surf comes after Norman.

## Wally outside the Gym
Speak to Wally at the Gym entrance and complete his battle and the following conversation. This is separate from Wattson's leader battle. Heal afterward if needed.

If the entrance scene has not cleared, talk to Wally again rather than searching for an alternative entrance. Verdanturf and Rusturf Tunnel are optional detours at this stage, not substitutes for the Gym event.

## Wattson and the Dynamo Badge
Inside the Gym, step on the floor switches to change the electric barriers. Look at which fences disappear before moving through; you do not take a damage penalty merely for having the puzzle in its unsolved state. Defeat trainers along the reachable path and approach Wattson.

Wattson specializes in Electric Pokémon. Ground attacks are especially useful, and a Ground Pokémon avoids ordinary Electric damage. Flying and Water team members need extra care. Magnemite-family opponents also have Steel typing, so a Fire or Fighting attack can help against those particular targets.

A main team around **level 23–25** is a suggested preparation range. Buy healing items, check move PP and save outside before committing to the leader. Do not assume a Water starter can handle this Gym by itself.

Victory earns the **Dynamo Badge** and **TM Shock Wave**. The badge unlocks **Rock Smash** in the field. Interact with a breakable rock; you do not need to assign the move to a party member.

## Head north onto Route 111
Take Mauville's northern exit. Use Rock Smash on the rocks blocking the road north. The Winstrate family's consecutive battles are optional; heal first if you choose to try them.

The desert farther north is still inaccessible without Go-Goggles. Turn toward Route 112 and Fiery Path for the current story route. You are heading toward Fallarbor and Meteor Falls before the path to Mt. Chimney fully opens.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Wally's Gym entrance encounter finished.
- Dynamo Badge earned and Rock Smash available.
- Bike selected, if you want one for travel.
- Northern Route 111 rocks cleared; team ready for the longer northern journey.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 7: Fallarbor, Meteor Falls and Mt. Chimney
articles.summary: Follow the northern route, find Professor Cozmo and stop Magma at the volcano.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Travel around the blocked desert to Fallarbor, witness the meteorite theft in Meteor Falls, then return to Mt. Chimney and stop Team Magma. Descend toward Lavaridge afterward.

This is a longer stretch between major story stops. Bring Potions, status cures and a few Repels if you want to avoid repeated cave encounters. Heal whenever you reach a town.

## Fiery Path to Route 113
1. From northern Route 111, turn west onto Route 112.
2. The cable car is blocked for now. Enter **Fiery Path** instead.
3. Cross the cave's main passage. Strength boulders mark optional areas you cannot fully explore yet; they do not block the ordinary crossing.
4. Emerge on the northern side of Route 112 and reconnect with Route 111 above the desert.
5. Continue north and west onto **Route 113**, following the ash-covered road into Fallarbor.

The ash landscape is part of the route's setting. You do not need to wait for a particular season or weather to advance.

## Fallarbor and Route 114
Heal in Fallarbor and resupply. **Optional:** Visit the nearby ash workshop and other houses, explore the Battle Tent, or collect side-route items. These are not required for the meteorite scene.

Leave west onto **Route 114**, then follow the route south toward **Meteor Falls**. Lanette's home and reachable wild catches are optional stops along the way. Use the correct map's list below; Route 113 and Route 114 have different encounter tables.

## The meteorite theft
Enter Meteor Falls from Route 114 and approach **Professor Cozmo** and Team Magma. Watch the scene involving both teams and finish the conversation. You do not need Waterfall or the deep postgame cave paths for this event.

After the scene, return toward Route 112. You can retrace Route 114, Fallarbor, Route 113 and Fiery Path, or use the available cave exit and mainland road as appropriate. Your destination is the **Route 112 cable-car station**, not the blocked desert.

If Magma still blocks the cable car, return to Meteor Falls and ensure the theft scene has actually played; merely entering the cave is not enough.

## Mt. Chimney
Ride the cable car to the summit. Follow the path through the ongoing team conflict and defeat Magma opponents blocking the way. Heal before speaking to **Maxie** at the meteorite machine.

A healthy team around **level 25–28** is a suggested starting point. Water and Ground coverage can help against Fire threats, but inspect the current opponent rather than using one move for every matchup. Keep a healthy backup in case your first choice is worn down.

After winning, finish the scene. **Optional:** Inspect the machine to recover the **Meteorite**. Professor Cozmo in Fallarbor can reward its return; that trip can wait.

## Jagged Pass to Lavaridge
Descend south through **Jagged Pass**. Bikes can access optional terrain, but the ordinary descending path leads toward Lavaridge. Do not expect to enter Magma's later hideout now; its opening belongs to a later story event.

Heal at Lavaridge and save. Your next badge is the Heat Badge.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Meteor Falls theft scene completed.
- Cable car unblocked and Mt. Chimney reached.
- Maxie defeated; summit scene finished.
- Jagged Pass descended and Lavaridge reached.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 8: Lavaridge and the desert
articles.summary: Earn the Heat Badge, receive Go-Goggles and prepare to return to Norman.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Defeat Flannery in Lavaridge, collect Go-Goggles from your rival and return toward Petalburg for your fifth badge. The desert is now an optional exploration area.

## Prepare in Lavaridge
Heal, save and buy appropriate healing items. The hot springs and herb shop are optional stops. **Optional:** Speak to the woman near the springs about her Pokémon Egg; keep a free party slot if you want to accept it.

Flannery's Fire team makes Water, Ground and Rock attacks useful, while Grass, Bug, Ice and Steel Pokémon can be vulnerable. An attack's type matters more than a Pokémon simply belonging to one of those types. Avoid bringing a team that all shares the same weakness.

A main team around **level 27–30** is suggested. Keep enough healing supplies for the Gym trainers as well as the leader.

## Flannery and the Heat Badge
The Gym uses holes and steam passages connecting its floors. Enter a hole, note where it leads and use the steam lifts to work upward. If you return to a familiar area, choose a different reachable passage rather than repeatedly taking the same loop.

Defeat the trainers you meet, then speak to Flannery. Fire attacks and setup moves can turn a worn-down team into an easy target; heal before the leader and avoid unnecessary switches that give her free turns.

Finish the reward conversation after winning. You receive the **Heat Badge** and **TM Overheat**. In Legends, the badge unlocks **Strength** for boulder puzzles without teaching an HM.

## Go-Goggles and the desert
Complete the rival scene outside the Gym to receive **Go-Goggles**. You can now enter Route 111's sandstorm desert.

**Optional:** Explore the desert for new catches, trainers and items. Mirage Tower, when present, offers the fossil choice; some floor challenges need the Mach Bike and Rock Smash. You can postpone that detour without blocking the main story. The desert's wild encounters are shown under Route 111, with the map and method information kept separate from nearby towns.

For a fossil reward, choose the one you want and later take it to the revival researcher at Devon Corporation in Rustboro. You do not need a fossil Pokémon for Norman.

## Return to Petalburg
With four badges, Norman is finally ready for your challenge. Retrace the mainland route toward Mauville, then use the western connection through Verdanturf and Rusturf Tunnel if you want a shorter return toward Rustboro.

In Rusturf Tunnel, Rock Smash can clear the rocks separating the two sides. Finish the reunion scene if you do it; the traditional **HM Strength** reward is optional for field use because your Heat Badge already unlocks that utility.

From Rustboro, travel south through Route 104 and Petalburg Woods, then east into Petalburg. Heal and save before the Gym. You have not unlocked Fly yet, so do not plan this trip around aerial travel.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Heat Badge earned; Strength field utility available.
- Rival's Go-Goggles conversation finished.
- Optional desert stops completed or deliberately postponed.
- Petalburg reached with four badges and a healthy party.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 9: Norman and the first Surf journey
articles.summary: Earn the Balance Badge and cross Route 118 toward eastern Hoenn.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Defeat Norman in Petalburg, complete the Surf gift scene and travel back to Mauville. Cross Route 118's water to begin the journey toward Fortree.

## Petalburg Gym
Heal and save before entering. Choose doors through the Gym's themed trainer rooms. Their signs explain battle styles such as speed, defense and item use; choose a route, win the required fights and continue toward Norman. You do not need to clear every alternate room to reach him.

Bring a healthy Fighting attacker or other reliable coverage against Normal types. Ghost Pokémon avoid ordinary Normal attacks, but this does not mean they are immune to every move on Norman's team. A main team around **level 30–32** is a suggested starting point.

Norman's Slaking can hit hard but has turns when **Truant** prevents it acting. If you have Protect or a suitable recovery move, plan around those turns. Avoid treating every quiet turn as permanent safety: the next attack can still be powerful.

## Balance Badge and Surf
1. Defeat Norman and finish the reward conversation for the **Balance Badge** and **TM Facade**.
2. Complete the scene with Wally's family. Follow it through to Wally's house and receive **HM Surf** from his father.
3. Heal and save after the event.

The Balance Badge unlocks **Surf** in Legends. Interact with a suitable water edge to use the field utility; no Pokémon needs to learn Surf. The HM is still a useful teachable battle move, so you may want to use it on a Water partner independently of field access.

## What Surf opens
You can now cross water on many earlier routes and revisit reachable islands or water-edge items. **Optional:** New Mauville and earlier fishing/Surf areas offer catches and side rewards. These detours can wait if you want to continue the story first.

Repels reduce ordinary encounters while travelling, but they do not replace healing or guarantee that a route has no battles. Keep track of your active Pokémon's level and remaining supplies.

## Cross Route 118
Return to **Mauville** by the mainland connections and leave east onto **Route 118**. Surf across the narrow water crossing. Land on the eastern shore and continue the story conversation with Steven when you meet him.

**Optional:** Speak to the fisherman on this route for the **Good Rod**. It opens additional encounter tables beyond your Old Rod catches. Use the route-specific lists rather than assuming every body of water contains the same Pokémon.

Follow the land north toward **Route 119**. Do not turn the long eastern road into an aimless search: Fortree lies beyond the Weather Institute and the northern part of Route 119.

## Ready for the Weather Institute
Before heading up Route 119, bring healing items, status cures and room for new catches. The route is longer than the small early-game routes. A team in the low thirties is a useful starting point, but your moves and coverage matter too.

- Five badges earned; Surf utility available.
- Wally's father's conversation completed.
- Eastern Route 118 reached.
- Northern path to Route 119 identified.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 10: The Weather Institute and Fortree
articles.summary: Rescue the researchers, obtain the Devon Scope and earn the Feather Badge.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Clear Team Aqua from the Weather Institute, reach Fortree, use Steven's Devon Scope to reveal the hidden obstruction and defeat Winona.

## Up Route 119
From eastern Route 118, head north through Route 119. Follow its paths and bridges, using Surf where the ordinary route requires a water crossing. Tall grass slows some travel options; walking is fine.

Wild catches and trainers can help you prepare, but heal before the Weather Institute. If your party is exhausted, use the institute's rest facilities when available instead of forcing several battles with low HP.

## Rescue the Weather Institute
Enter the building occupied by Team Aqua. Defeat the grunts blocking the stairs and clear the upstairs confrontation with Aqua's administrator. Finish the researchers' conversation.

They offer **Castform**, a gift Pokémon. Keep a free party slot for a straightforward handoff; if your party is full, the gift can be sent to storage, provided there is space. The ordinary Route 119 wild list does not include this gift as a grass encounter.

Complete the scene before leaving. If the nearby crossing is still obstructed, check for an unfinished upstairs conversation.

## Rival battle and Fortree
Cross the bridge beyond the institute and continue north. Your rival interrupts the journey with another battle. Heal first and prepare for your save's chosen starter matchup. Finish the conversation afterward to receive **HM Fly**.

You cannot use Fly in the field yet: it needs Winona's Feather Badge. Continue on foot into **Fortree**, heal and explore the treehouse paths.

Fortree Gym's entrance is blocked by an unseen Pokémon. It is a story obstruction, not a collision bug or a reason to restart your save.

## Steven and the Devon Scope
1. Leave Fortree east onto **Route 120**.
2. Follow the route to Steven at the bridge.
3. Complete his demonstration and the encounter with the revealed Kecleon.
4. Finish the conversation to receive the **Devon Scope**.
5. Return to Fortree's blocked Gym approach and interact with the obstruction using the new item.

Kecleon is a revealed special encounter, separate from the routine wild table. Save before interacting if you want a catching checkpoint, and have Poké Balls ready.

## Winona and the Feather Badge
Work through the Gym's rotating gate puzzle, approaching gates from different sides when a path is blocked. Defeat the trainers and heal before Winona.

Electric, Rock and Ice attacks can be useful against Flying opponents, but secondary types matter. A Ground/Flying Pokémon avoids Electric damage; a Dragon/Flying target is especially vulnerable to Ice. Avoid assuming one Electric attack covers the entire Gym.

A team around **level 33–35** is suggested. Winona's setup moves can snowball, so use your strongest suitable attacks and keep healthy alternatives available.

Victory earns the **Feather Badge** and **TM Aerial Ace**. Fly is now available through FIELD without teaching the HM, which makes returning to previously visited towns much easier.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Weather Institute cleared and gift conversation completed.
- Rival battle finished; HM Fly collected.
- Devon Scope received and Gym obstruction removed.
- Feather Badge earned; next destination is Route 120 toward Lilycove.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 11: Lilycove, the stolen orbs and the hideouts
articles.summary: Follow Aqua to Mt. Pyre, clear Magma’s hideout and reopen the eastern sea route.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Reach Lilycove, investigate Mt. Pyre, open the Magma Hideout with the Magma Emblem, witness the submarine theft in Slateport and clear Aqua's Lilycove hideout. This sequence opens the sea route to Mossdeep.

## Routes 120 and 121 to Lilycove
Continue east and south along Route 120, then east onto Route 121. Follow bridges and the main paths toward **Lilycove**. The Safari Zone is an optional catching stop; it does not replace the Mt. Pyre story event.

Heal in Lilycove. **Optional:** Battle your rival near the department store and resupply afterward. The city's harbour and department store are landmarks, but the Aqua hideout will not fully advance before the preceding story events.

## Mt. Pyre and the Magma Emblem
1. Return to Route 121 and use its southern water connection onto **Route 122**.
2. Surf to **Mt. Pyre** and enter the building.
3. Take the exit leading onto the mountain's exterior, then climb toward the summit. The interior grave floors contain optional trainers and items; the summit confrontation is outside.
4. Clear the Aqua opponents on the ascent and watch the summit scene.
5. Speak to the elderly couple and finish the explanation about the stolen orbs. Receive the **Magma Emblem**.

Save after the scene. Route 123 and the interior tower floors can be explored separately; you do not need to clear every side area to unlock the next hideout.

## Magma Hideout beneath Jagged Pass
Return to the Mt. Chimney area, ride the cable car and descend **Jagged Pass**. The Magma Emblem opens the concealed hideout entrance when you approach the relevant rock along the pass.

Enter and follow the cave passages downward. Use your badge-based Strength utility for boulders where needed. Fight the trainers blocking progress, watch your supplies and save before the deepest confrontation with **Maxie**.

Finish the Groudon awakening scene and Maxie's conversation. The target here is completing the hideout story, not catching Groudon during this scene. Return to the entrance and heal in a town.

A healthy team in the **high thirties** is a preparation suggestion for this chain. Bring coverage for more than Fire types, since the teams also use other Pokémon.

## Slateport's submarine theft
Fly to **Slateport** and visit the harbour where Captain Stern is being interviewed. Speak to him and complete the event involving Team Aqua and the submarine.

This event is required before the Lilycove hideout's departure sequence. If you find Aqua's base has not progressed, check that both Maxie's deep hideout event and Stern's harbour scene have finished.

## Aqua Hideout in Lilycove
Return to Lilycove and Surf to the hideout entrance northeast of the city. Work through its warp pads and branching rooms. Treat each pad as a connection: note where it arrives, and return by the available pad if you reach an optional dead end.

**Optional but useful:** Explore the item room containing the **Master Ball** before finishing the hideout. Some nearby apparent item balls are Pokémon encounters, so keep your team healthy. The Master Ball is valuable but not required to clear the base.

Reach the submarine area, defeat the Aqua administrator guarding it and finish the escape scene. The Wailmer obstruction on the eastern sea route then clears. Leave, heal in Lilycove and save before the crossing.

## Ready for Mossdeep
Surf east onto **Route 124** and continue toward Mossdeep. This ocean crossing is the next main route; Mt. Pyre and the two hideouts were the prerequisites.

- Magma Emblem received at Mt. Pyre.
- Maxie's awakening scene completed.
- Stern's submarine-theft scene completed.
- Aqua hideout escape finished; eastern sea route open.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 12: Mossdeep and the Mind Badge
articles.summary: Win the double-battle Gym, help Steven at the Space Center and unlock Dive.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Cross Route 124, earn the Mind Badge from Tate and Liza, stop Magma at the Space Center and complete Steven's Dive gift scene.

## Route 124 to Mossdeep
From Lilycove, Surf east across **Route 124**. Follow the ocean route into Mossdeep and heal. Islands, divers' services and nearby water catches are optional stops; underwater areas require Dive, which this chapter unlocks.

**Optional:** Collect the **Super Rod** from the fisherman in Mossdeep's house. This expands your fishing choices again. Route 125 and Shoal Cave north of the city are optional detours; cave access and available rooms can depend on the tide, so do not confuse a closed route with the main story destination.

## Prepare two reliable battlers
Mossdeep Gym uses **double battles**. Have at least two healthy Pokémon ready, and check that their attacks and abilities work sensibly together. Moves that strike both sides can also hit your own partner; read the move description before choosing one.

Tate and Liza specialize in Psychic Pokémon. Dark and Ghost attacks can help; certain Rock/Psychic opponents also dislike Water and Grass coverage. Ground immunity and other secondary-type interactions mean one blanket strategy will not cover every enemy.

A trained team around **level 40–43** is suggested. Bring healing supplies and avoid relying on one strong Pokémon while the second faints immediately.

## Tate and Liza
Use the Gym's floor mechanisms to change the routes and platform positions. Return to a reachable switch if the next path is blocked, then check which connection moved. Defeat the Gym trainers and approach the leaders with two usable battlers.

During the leader fight, remove dangerous threats rather than splitting damage without a purpose. Keep both partners healthy when possible, and watch for opponents setting up stronger attacks.

Finish the reward conversation to receive the **Mind Badge** and **TM Calm Mind**. The badge unlocks **Dive** as a field utility in Legends. Story conversations still matter even though you do not need a learned HM to use the utility.

## The Space Center crisis
Follow the city story to the **Space Center**. Defeat the Magma opponents inside and make your way upstairs. When Steven offers a joint battle, select the Pokémon you want to contribute and complete the fight against the Magma leaders.

Heal between available encounters if needed. Finish the post-battle conversation rather than leaving as soon as the battle screen closes.

## Steven's house and Dive
Visit **Steven's house** in Mossdeep after the Space Center event. Complete his conversation to receive **HM Dive** and the explanation about deep water.

Dark-blue sea patches mark Dive terrain. Use the contextual utility there to descend; underwater openings and suitable surface exits connect the two map layers. Ordinary light-blue water is not a Dive entry point.

**Optional:** Explore reachable underwater items or water catches once prepared. For the next main story objective, head south toward **Route 128** and the underwater entrance to Seafloor Cavern.

## End-of-chapter checklist
- Mind Badge earned with a prepared double-battle team.
- Space Center Magma encounter completed with Steven.
- Steven's house conversation and Dive gift completed.
- Supplies replenished for the underwater journey and Seafloor Cavern.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 13: Sootopolis, Rayquaza and the final badge
articles.summary: Clear Seafloor Cavern, resolve the legendary crisis and defeat Juan.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Follow the stolen submarine to Seafloor Cavern, complete the Sootopolis crisis by meeting Rayquaza at Sky Pillar, then earn Juan's Rain Badge. This opens the final route to the League.

## Route 128 and Seafloor Cavern
Surf south from Mossdeep through Route 127 toward **Route 128**. Dive at the deep-water patch connected to the cavern entrance, find the underwater opening and surface inside the entrance area where the stolen submarine is docked.

Enter **Seafloor Cavern** and work through the rooms. Rock Smash clears breakable rocks; Strength moves the boulders. Activate the utility when required rather than assuming a taught HM is missing. Current rooms use their water flow to move you between landing points; try a different entry point if a current sends you back.

For boulder puzzles, plan a route before pushing a stone against a wall. A trapped boulder can usually be reset by leaving and re-entering the room. You do not need to clear every optional floor tile to reach the next exit.

Heal and save before the deepest Aqua confrontation with **Archie**. A healthy team around **level 42–45** is a suggested starting point. Finish the Kyogre awakening and following story scenes; this is not the normal catching opportunity for Kyogre.

## Enter Sootopolis
Return to the sea and reach **Route 126**, the water surrounding Sootopolis's crater. Dive at the appropriate deep-water area, enter the underwater opening into the crater and surface inside **Sootopolis City**.

Heal and follow Steven's directions during the abnormal weather crisis. The Gym is blocked until the crisis is resolved. Go to the **Cave of Origin** with the story characters and speak to **Wallace**. When the conversation asks where Rayquaza may be found, choose **Sky Pillar**.

Do not search the Cave of Origin for a required Kyogre capture. Your current objective is finding Rayquaza and completing the story scenes.

## Sky Pillar
Travel toward **Route 131**, near Pacifidlog. Surf to Sky Pillar's northern entrance and meet Wallace there. Complete his conversation and enter the tower.

Climb to the summit using the accessible story path and awaken **Rayquaza**. The initial crisis visit is distinct from a later catching revisit: the damaged-floor Mach Bike challenge associated with revisiting the tower should not be treated as a prerequisite for the first story ascent.

After Rayquaza leaves, return to Sootopolis. Fly is a convenient way back now that you have the Feather Badge. Finish the legendary confrontation scene and speak to the relevant characters outside the Gym until the doorway is available.

## Juan and the Rain Badge
Heal, save and enter the Gym. Its ice-floor puzzle requires stepping across the puzzle's ice tiles without retracing a cracked tile. Falling sends you to the lower trainer area; return upstairs to attempt the floor again. Pause and plan the next turn before committing to a tile.

Juan specializes in Water Pokémon. Grass and Electric coverage are useful, but Water/Ground targets avoid Electric attacks. His Kingdra's Water/Dragon typing does not share the same simple weakness as a pure Water Pokémon; a strong neutral move, Dragon or Fairy coverage can be useful depending on your team.

A main team around **level 44–47** is suggested. Keep healing items and enough move PP for a longer fight. Finish the reward conversation for the **Rain Badge** and **TM Water Pulse**.

## Waterfall and the League route
Complete Wallace's post-crisis conversation for **HM Waterfall** if you have not collected it already. Legends' field use is unlocked by the Rain Badge, so you do not need to teach the HM to climb valid waterfalls.

Heal and save. Your next destination is **Ever Grande City**, reached from the eastern sea routes and the waterfall at its southern approach.

- Archie and the Seafloor Cavern awakening completed.
- Wallace met in the Cave of Origin; Sky Pillar story visit completed.
- Sootopolis crisis resolved and Juan defeated.
- Eight badges earned; Waterfall utility available.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Chapter 14: Victory Road and the Hoenn League
articles.summary: Reach Ever Grande, cross Victory Road and become Hoenn Champion.
articles.content:
## Your goal
Use Waterfall to reach Ever Grande, pass Wally and Victory Road, then defeat the Elite Four and Champion Wallace. This completes the main Hoenn story.

## Prepare for Ever Grande
Resupply before the final route. Bring strong healing items, Revives, status cures and PP-restoring items you have collected. Once you begin the Elite Four sequence, you cannot use a Pokémon Center between members.

Check held items and moves. A balanced team should have answers for Dark, Ghost, Ice, Dragon and Water opponents. This does not require five separate specialist Pokémon, but it does require more than repeatedly choosing your starter's first attack.

A main team around **level 50–55**, with stronger preparation for the Champion, is a suggested starting point rather than a level cap. If your team struggles, train on reachable routes or in Victory Road and return when ready.

## Ever Grande and Victory Road
1. Surf toward **Ever Grande City's southern approach** from Route 128.
2. Use Waterfall at the city's entrance waterfall.
3. Heal at the Pokémon Center and save before entering **Victory Road**.
4. Prepare for **Wally's battle** near the start of the cave journey. He now has a full team; finish the conversation after winning.
5. Follow the ladders and cave passages toward the northern exit.

The cave combines dark floors, boulders, breakable rocks and water crossings. Use FIELD → Flash for visibility and your badge utilities for Strength, Rock Smash, Surf and Waterfall as the terrain requires. You do not need to rebuild your party around HM moveslots.

The inline encounter lists distinguish Victory Road's floors. Repels can help you travel, but trainer battles and Wally still need a healthy team. If a boulder gets trapped, leave and re-enter that room to reset its arrangement.

## The League checkpoint
Exit into northern Ever Grande and enter the League building. Heal, buy supplies and make any final party changes before passing the guards. Save here so you have a clean preparation checkpoint.

Confirm that all eight badge events are complete. Skipping Winona earlier does not let you ignore her badge at the League entrance. The walkthrough follows the full intended badge order.

## The Elite Four
Challenge the members in their fixed sequence:

1. **Sidney — Dark:** Fighting, Bug and Fairy coverage can help. Check secondary types before assuming one attack is always best.
2. **Phoebe — Ghost:** Dark and Ghost attacks are useful. Normal and Fighting attacks usually fail against Ghost targets without a specific effect that changes that interaction.
3. **Glacia — Ice:** Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel coverage can help, but several opponents also have Water typing. Avoid sending a Fire partner into an unfavourable Water attack without a plan.
4. **Drake — Dragon:** Ice, Dragon and Fairy coverage are useful. Dragon attacks also threaten your own Dragon partners, and some enemies' secondary types change their weaknesses.

After each battle, use your Bag to restore HP, revive fainted partners, cure status and replenish important moves when needed. Check the whole party before entering the next room; do not leave a needed backup fainted just because the last opponent is defeated.

## Champion Wallace
Wallace is Emerald's Champion; Steven is not the final League opponent in this story. His Water-focused team calls for good Grass and Electric coverage, but Water/Ground and other dual types need individual answers.

Heal and restore move PP before approaching him. Choose targets carefully, watch for setup or recovery, and keep a backup capable of finishing a weakened opponent. If you lose, adjust moves, held items or levels rather than assuming the first attempt was a permanent failure.

After winning, finish the Hall of Fame scene and credits. Continue your save afterward: the ending does not delete your party or require a new game.

## After becoming Champion
You can return to optional Hoenn areas, complete the Pokédex and explore the current postgame. [[kanto|Read the Kanto overview]] for Legends' regional expansion and entry instructions. Kanto's developing story is separate from these fourteen Hoenn chapters and will receive its own manually reviewed walkthrough.

- Victory Road crossed and all eight badges confirmed.
- Elite Four defeated in order.
- Wallace defeated; Hall of Fame and ending completed.
- Continued save ready for optional Hoenn and Legends postgame content.

Checked against Legends v0.0.31.1. Suggested training levels are advice; wild lists use the wiki’s existing manually maintained encounter snapshot.

articles.title: Options menu and saved preferences
articles.summary: A quick reference for the game’s configurable mechanics.
articles.content:
## Navigating the pages
The Options menu has **General**, **Legends**, and **Adventure** pages. Choose NEXT PAGE and press A, or press L/R, to switch pages. Use Left/Right to change most values; B saves and exits. The menu also displays the Legends version.

## Notable settings
- **EXP SHARE:** toggle the physical Key Item's party-wide experience effect.
- **FOLLOWER:** show or hide your lead eligible Pokémon behind you.
- **SHINY RATE:** choose 1/8192, 1/5680, or 1/1226 for ordinary wild generation.
- **SEASONS:** use real-calendar seasons or a seven-hour gameplay cycle.
- **SET SEASON:** available during the seven-hour gameplay mode.
- **STARTERS:** choose generations 1–9, Special, or Random for a **new game**.

## Before you start
Title-screen preferences can carry into New Game. Once you open the rescue bag on Route 101, the starter lineup and corresponding rival lineage are locked for that save. Changing STARTERS later does not rewrite an existing team.

More detailed guides: [[exp|EXP Share]], [[starters|Starters]], [[shiny|Shiny odds]], [[seasons|Seasons]], and [[followers|Followers]].

articles.title: EXP Share and Lucky Egg
articles.summary: How modernized party experience works and what Rustboro rewards.
articles.content:
## Party-wide experience
Legends uses the expansion's Gen 6-style EXP Share. It is a **Key Item**, supplied at the start of a new game and restored to qualifying older saves.

When switched **ON**:
- Battle participants receive their normal full EXP.
- Eligible non-participating party Pokémon receive a half share.
- Eggs receive no EXP.

When **OFF**, other party members do not receive the global share. The Key Item and the Legends Options setting change the same saved preference.

## Lucky Egg
Lucky Egg remains a separate held item with its normal EXP multiplier handling. When you deliver Mr. Stone's Letter to Steven and later report back to Devon Corporation in Rustboro, the reward is now a **Lucky Egg**, not an additional held Exp. Share.

Other EXP systems such as traded bonuses and scaled experience still use the expansion's native battle processing.

articles.title: Field moves without HM moveslots
articles.summary: Keep Emerald’s badge gates while freeing up moveslots.
articles.content:
## The core rule
You can use Emerald's eight required field utilities once you have the appropriate badge, **without teaching the HM to a party Pokémon**. Badges, valid terrain and story restrictions still matter.

| Utility | Required badge |
| --- | --- |
| Cut | Stone |
| Flash | Knuckle |
| Rock Smash | Dynamo |
| Strength | Heat |
| Surf | Balance |
| Fly | Feather |
| Dive | Mind |
| Waterfall | Rain |

## Using them
Interact with the familiar trees, rocks, boulders, shorelines, waterfalls and dive spots. The Pokémon party menu also gains a compact **FIELD** entry after you unlock a utility, which provides actions such as Flash and Fly.

Dig, Teleport, Sweet Scent, Secret Power and other Pokémon-specific field moves still follow the normal learned-move rules. HM attacks still exist as moves you can teach for battling.

articles.title: Starter Pokémon and rival teams
articles.summary: All starter modes, including special and random trios.
articles.content:
## Choose your set
Under Adventure Options, STARTERS defaults to GEN 3.

| Setting | Starter trio |
| --- | --- |
| GEN 1 | Bulbasaur / Charmander / Squirtle |
| GEN 2 | Chikorita / Cyndaquil / Totodile |
| GEN 3 | Treecko / Torchic / Mudkip |
| GEN 4 | Turtwig / Chimchar / Piplup |
| GEN 5 | Snivy / Tepig / Oshawott |
| GEN 6 | Chespin / Fennekin / Froakie |
| GEN 7 | Rowlet / Litten / Popplio |
| GEN 8 | Grookey / Scorbunny / Sobble |
| GEN 9 | Sprigatito / Fuecoco / Quaxly |
| SPECIAL | Happiny / Wattrel / Mankey |
| RANDOM | Three distinct eligible unevolved Pokémon |

## How rivals work
Generation sets select the rival's counter from the chosen generation. Special and Random use **Zorua**, evolving into Zoroark at level 30. The Random trio is rolled once when the Route 101 bag first opens; merely moving the selection cursor or declining does not reroll it.

The selected trio is fixed for the current save once the bag opens. Existing saves keep their established party and Gen 3 rival lineage.

articles.title: Shiny rates and special cases
articles.summary: Understand the selectable base odds and their limits.
articles.content:
## Three wild rates
From Legends Options, select **1/8192** (default), **1/5680**, or **1/1226**. This setting affects newly generated ordinary wild Pokémon, including grass, water, fishing and DexNav searches.

Additional eligible shiny rolls from Shiny Charm, chain fishing and DexNav may improve actual encounter odds beyond the selected base value.

## Important exclusions
Changing the option does **not** retroactively change your party or PC. Eggs, gifts, trainer Pokémon, scripted and roaming encounters use their own existing logic unless a feature specifically states otherwise.

The one-time [[da-bug|Da Bug PC gift]] has an independent **1-in-10** shiny roll. That exception is not a global shiny-odds change.

articles.title: National Pokédex and Champion reward
articles.summary: Earlier National Mode and a more useful postgame reward.
articles.content:
## National Mode early
Professor Birch enables National Pokédex Mode at the first ordinary Pokédex handoff. You do not need to finish the Elite Four to unlock it.

## After becoming Champion
The original National Dex upgrade event is repurposed. Birch instead awards **25 Rare Candies**. If your Bag is full, the reward follows the project's fallback storage/deferred-delivery handling.

These changes retain the core Emerald story progression while allowing expanded species access earlier.

articles.title: Overworld Pokémon followers
articles.summary: Choose whether your lead Pokémon accompanies you.
articles.content:
## Who follows?
With FOLLOWER set to ON (the default), the first conscious non-Egg Pokémon in your party follows you. Reorder your team to change the follower. No Pokémon appears before receiving a starter, when your whole party is fainted, or when only Eggs are present.

## Player control
Use Legends Options to switch FOLLOWER ON or OFF. Save to keep the preference. Title-screen choices carry into New Game.

## When a follower disappears
Certain cutscenes, forced movement, cramped interiors, travel states and maps with no free object slot temporarily hide followers. This is normal behavior rather than a reset of your selected preference. The game reuses pokeemerald-expansion's native follower graphics and movement systems.

articles.title: Seasons and foliage
articles.summary: How spring, summer, autumn, and winter are selected.
articles.content:
## Two season modes
**REAL TIME** (default) follows the RTC calendar's Northern Hemisphere seasons: March–May spring; June–August summer; September–November autumn; December–February winter.

**7H PLAY** advances Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter, seven recorded game hours each. Four seasons repeat every 28 gameplay hours. Time in menus and battles counts; time with the game closed does not.

## Controlling a season
Choose SEASONS on Legends Options. In 7H PLAY mode, **SET SEASON** lets you restart the selected season's timer. The change appears after a faded map reload or save reload, not instantly while standing outdoors.

## Visual changes
Vegetation changes from spring and summer greens to autumn amber and winter frost. Regional weather patterns vary by season; Kanto grass and trees and ordinary outdoor grass battle backgrounds follow seasonal colors. Special locations, protected graphics, water, and story-driven weather are preserved.

If your emulator's RTC is unavailable, real-calendar mode falls back to the saved gameplay cycle. See [[clock|Clocks]] and [[weather|Dynamic weather]].

articles.title: Dynamic weather
articles.summary: Regional forecasts, special-weather protections, and seasons.
articles.content:
## Ordinary outdoor forecasts
Legends brings changing weather to suitable outdoor areas of Hoenn and Kanto. The forecast advances in recorded gameplay time and varies by region, time of day and season.

Depending on the location, you may see rain, occasional storms, fog, or winter upland snow. Inland, coastal and highland areas do not share identical forecasts. Coastal Kanto does not randomly snow.

## Story weather stays intact
Special effects such as Emerald's Groudon/Kyogre crisis, region-specific event weather and indoor environments retain their scripted behavior.

The older generic SUNNY CLOUDS pattern was deliberately removed because the native effect could appear through map geometry elsewhere. A clear forecast may be substituted instead.

articles.title: Bedroom clock and pause display
articles.summary: Understand real time, manual time, and the fallback clock.
articles.content:
## Your bedroom clock
At the first bedroom clock event and on later visits, choose:
- **REAL TIME** (default): the emulator/device RTC when available.
- **MANUAL**: set the analog bedroom clock yourself.

The rival's bedroom clock is for viewing only. The first visit confirms the selected clock instead of adding the old introductory offset.

## Without emulator RTC
The clock falls back to **9:00 AM plus recorded playtime**. It persists across ordinary saves and continues beyond the native 999-hour display limit. Re-enabling a valid RTC returns REAL TIME to the device clock.

## Start-menu display
The pause panel shows a live clock, season and weather. It updates on minute changes while the emulator is running, including while the pause menu is open. A fully paused emulator cannot update the display until resumed.

The Adventure Log's played-day counter tracks actual distinct play dates and does not count skipped dates. See [[journal|Adventure Log]].

articles.title: Trainer appearance at New Game
articles.summary: Five skin tones and five outfits, with live previews.
articles.content:
## Character creation
After choosing a trainer gender during Professor Birch's introduction, select one of five skin tones and one of five outfits. A live sprite preview appears alongside the selection.

| Outfit | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Emerald | Original Emerald-style look |
| Trail | Jacket and trousers |
| Sport | Striped shirt and shorts |
| Yellow | Yellow-colored style |
| Lavender | Lavender design with a cream neck detail |

Selections apply across normal overworld movement, local trainer presentation and your Trainer Card.

## Changing your style later
Visit the [[wardrobe|wardrobe]] in your Littleroot bedroom or buy a placeable wardrobe for your secret base. Existing saves retain their original look until you make a new selection.

Magma and Aqua are full costumes rather than ordinary recolored shirts. Dive keeps the native covered suit.

articles.title: Wardrobe, costumes, and footwear
articles.summary: The full outfit editor: shoes, boots, scarves, jackets, and costumes.
articles.content:
## Finding the wardrobe
A small storage box sits directly beneath your bed in Littleroot Town. Face it from an adjacent tile and press A to open your wardrobe. You can also purchase a placeable wardrobe decoration for ₽3,000 from Pretty Petal Flower Shop on Route 104 and place it in your own secret base.

## Navigating
Up/Down scroll the categories (six visible at once). Left/Right changes the highlighted option. Select **APPLY** to save or **CANCEL** / B to discard. Preview updates before you commit.

| Category | Available choices |
| --- | --- |
| OUTFIT | Emerald, Trail, Sport, Yellow, Lavender |
| COSTUMES | None, Team Magma, Team Aqua |
| SCARF | None, Crimson, Ocean, Emerald, Lavender, Cream |
| JACKET | None, Navy |
| SHOES | Original, Red, Blue, Green, White, Purple, Light-brown boots, Black boots |
| TRAINER CARD | Original, Emerald, Ocean, Crimson, Lavender, Gold, Rose, Slate |

The tall-shaft boots are visually distinct from the shoes in their preview and applicable overworld poses. Magma and Aqua use their own complete grunt uniforms, with their fixed costume accessories and footwear. Your previous appearance remains stored when you take a costume off.

[[trainer-card|Trainer Card colors]] have a separate explanation.

articles.title: Trainer Card customization
articles.summary: Eight card backgrounds, including the original.
articles.content:
## Choose your card
In the bedroom or secret-base [[wardrobe|wardrobe]], scroll to TRAINER CARD and select Original, Emerald, Ocean, Crimson, Lavender, Gold, Rose, or Slate. A small live color swatch accompanies the wardrobe preview.

Choose APPLY to commit the new design. CANCEL or B preserves the previous card color.

## What stays the same?
Your badge display, Trainer Card stars and card information follow the existing game rules. The styling applies to your own local Trainer Card without altering remote link-card data.

articles.title: DexNav
articles.summary: Finding encounters, forgiving approaches, and terrain guidance.
articles.content:
## Unlock
DexNav becomes available with Professor Birch's first Pokédex gift. Players returning from older saves with a Pokédex gain it automatically when they continue.

## Searching
Select DexNav from the Start menu. Nearby wild-encounter terrain and actual encounter tables must be present. When there is no valid search area, a small upper-left guide explains where DexNav works; dismiss it with A, B or START.

## Approaching a target
Searching a Pokémon does **not** fail merely because you walk, run or cycle toward it. The target times out after **45 seconds**, rather than the earlier 15-second limit. Going out of signal range, manually cancelling, leaving the map, or letting the timer expire can still end a search. Reach the target to enter the normal battle.

[[shiny|Selectable shiny rates]] also apply to eligible newly generated DexNav encounters.

articles.title: Adventure Log and played days
articles.summary: A notebook of milestones, catches, and dates actually played.
articles.content:
## Open the notebook
Choose **ADVENTURE LOG** from the Start menu. It resembles a cream-and-lavender field notebook and stores up to **32 recent entries** including story milestones, locations, and one recent captured Pokémon with its level where available.

## Controls
- **Left/Right or L/R:** flip older/newer pages.
- **SELECT:** change All, Day, and Story filters.
- **Up/Down:** browse available played days in Day mode.
- **A:** return to the newest page in the active filter.
- **B or START:** close the notebook back to the pause menu.

## DAY counter
